metadata.prompt: A sleek, black mouse cursor hovering inches away from a vibrant, pulsing green button that says 'SECURE DATA ACCESS'.
A crisp corporate logo that begins to blur and fragment into jagged red digital shards.
A 3D view of two identical-looking office buildings; one is solid, the other is a hollow, pixelated facade.
A glowing URL bar displaying portal.microsoft-verify.io. The .io is highlighted with a harsh, red spotlight.
A macro view of the word PAYPAL. The second P is slowly replaced by a Greek Rho character that looks identical.
A kinetic animation of a mouse cursor moving in slow motion towards a blue hyperlink.
A digital highlighting of the bottom-left corner of a web browser, showing a raw URL string in bright white text.
A blue button labeled 'SIGN IN' that has a glowing red electrical wire snaking out from behind it into a dark hole.
A futuristic robotic arm holding a digital clipboard, checking off items under the heading 'URL VALIDATION'.
A dark void with three glowing portals labeled Link A, Link B, and Link C. Two are unstable and red.
A semi-transparent blue hex-shield appearing over a standard corporate login field.

content.narrative: You’ve analyzed the sender. You’ve resisted the emotional subject line. Now, the attacker presents the final obstacle: The Payload. They want you to click. Everything in the email—the professional tone, the urgent prompt—is a delivery vehicle for a single string of malicious characters. The most common payload is a link to a Fake Login Page. Attackers are masters of world-building. They use Typosquatting—creating domains that look identical to a legitimate portal. In the digital world, close enough is a disaster. The defense is a manual override: The Hover. If your mouse moves, your eyes must move to the status bar in the corner of your screen. If the destination doesn't match the description, the link is a trap. We are going to run a simulation. I will present three links. You will audit them. The machine does not make mistakes. Neither should you. Initiate simulation.
content.persona_direction: Rogue AI (The Glitch) - Cold, tactical, instructive.
content.speaker: Rogue AI

content: Secondary Step: Fake Login Portals (Credential Harvesting)

content.question: What is the primary purpose of 'Typosquatting'?
options: To fix spelling errors in official emails.
To register domains that look almost identical to legitimate ones.
content.correct_answer: To register domains that look almost identical to legitimate ones.
